resources.title: Python for Data Analysis, 3rd edition
resources.author: Wes McKinney
resources.prerequisites: Basic Python syntax; diagnose gaps first
resources.why: Free author edition with practical data cleaning; selective review avoids another full beginner course.
resources.compatibility: Book uses an older pandas environment. Pin a working environment and check current pandas documentation before replacing deprecated APIs; do not assume every snippet works on the latest release.

sections.title: Ch. 8 and 12: trees and unsupervised learning

sections.title: Ch. 7–9: regression, exponential smoothing and ARIMA

resources.title: MIT 6.172 Performance Engineering of Software Systems
resources.author: Charles Leiserson and Julian Shun (MIT OpenCourseWare)
resources.prerequisites: C/C++, algorithms, basic CPU architecture; attempt after SC1008/SC2001-level foundations
resources.why: Fills the roadmap's clearest technical gap: measured performance engineering. Use selected labs/lectures, not the whole 18-unit MIT course.

sections.title: Lectures 1 and 10: measurement, profiling and reproducibility
sections.exercise: Benchmark a deterministic parser or array operation: record compiler, flags, CPU, input distribution, warmup, monotonic timing, repeated raw samples and p50/p95/p99; identify measurement overhead.

sections.title: Lectures 11 and 14–15: allocation and cache-aware algorithms
sections.exercise: Profile array-of-structures versus structure-of-arrays on fixed synthetic inputs. Predict cache/allocation effects, verify semantics, and publish reproducible before/after distributions.

sections.title: Lectures 16–17: parallelism and synchronisation overhead
sections.exercise: Compare single-thread and bounded-queue implementations with sanitizers and correctness assertions. Measure throughput and tail latency as load rises, including overload and shutdown behavior.
